This story isn't going to be about Mid-Tour leave, but the journey to mid-tour leave...

I was the last person in my company to take mid-tour leave. I didn't really have anything I was going back to, so if someone needed to trade slots with me, I'd let them. One buddy, his wife had a miscarriage, another buddy's first child was being born. No problem, take my slot.

We were about 9-10 month in to a 12 month deployment in Iraq. Finally, there was no one left waiting to go on leave, so it was me, and me alone, from my company.

I caught a ride from another platoon to the main FOB in our area. From there, I had to ride in the back of a 5 ton with no armor with about a dozen pogues I never met before. I accepted that if we took contact, I would be dead, and I was ok with that at this particular juncture in my life. We get to FOB Anaconda, the major hub for the US military in our area.

I make friends with someone who's in the same battalion as me, but he's a mechanic from Charlie company, and that's still cool in my book, they fix our vehicles. If he had been any other MOS besides 11B, track vehicle mechanic, or medic, I would've told him to fuck off. We're waiting for a chinook flight to BIAP, and just hang out until it's time to go.

He tells me about him having to possibly have to kill a dude in the prep for the Battle of Samarra. You see, we drove out there, staged to invade the city, left, and came back the next fucking night and invaded the city. When we left the first time, his truck wouldn't start, and they had no comms. Way back then, not every vehicle had a radio in it. So him and another mechanic are just stuck in the dust, watching the whole fucking battalion leave them behind. It gets to dusk, and this car with two Iraqis pulls over, and starts yelling at them. He gets out of the truck, and says hey, I don't know what you're saying, and the Iraqi starts yelling at him, so he's like fuck this, and starts shooting at the car and the two guys. There's a US Army patrol driving by, and they see him shooting at these guys, and they lay into the Iraqis with the .50 cal, destroying them. They patrol was infantry, so they search the car, find a bunch of small arms, which they shouldn't have had. I asked the mechanic if he killed either of the dudes, and he was just like, "I don't know, I haven't even zeroed my weapon".

We board the chinook at night, and it's like a 3 hour flight to BIAP. About 30 minutes into the flight, we start taking small arms fire, and every gunner on the chinook is laying down fire on the ground below. You could see out the window the other bird flying with us laying down trails of tracers. This was a wee bit scary because 2 weeks before a chinook got shot down with 15 soldiers heading home on leave. The mechanic yells to me, well because you can only yell into the person next to you's ear to say anything, "WHY ARE THEY SHOOTING?!?!?". He motioned towards the two door gunners. I yell back, "WE'RE BEING SHOT AT!! WE'RE GOING TO BE SHOT DOWN, AND THERE'S NOTHING YOU CAN DO ABOUT IT!!!"

"OH FUCK!!!"

Oh, man, he put his head down, and I was just dying laughing.

We get to BIAP, fly into Kuwait, no issues. From there I lose my mechanic buddy because he was flying into the East Coast hub, New York I think, and I was flying into Dallas. All and all, it took me about 3 days to get from my FOB to Kuwait, and onto a plane to Dallas.

On the plane, I'm sitting next to this guy from a much smaller unit. His MOS and unit got slotted for a full size unit's mid tour leave, so this was his second mid tour leave this deployment. He was just like, I'm not complaining.

We land in Dallas, airplane taxis in under the firetrucks spraying the arches over it. My heart was racing, my eyes were slightly tearing for my brothers that would never get to see this, and my knees were loose. We all stand up, grab our bags, and everyone is lined up to exit the plane. My plane ride buddy is standing in front of me, and just before the door opens, he looks over his shoulder and says, "Just remember, don't look them in the eyes."

The door opens, all the soldiers stream out of the plane, fuck fuck fuck, there's a gauntlet of people waiting and cheering. I push my way through the crowd, some woman pulls me aside and kisses me on the cheek, i just drive on while another person hugs me. I give the man in a wheelchair a handshake, and push clear of the crowd. It was only about 50 civilians, but Jesus, it felt like I was being sufficated, and how the fuck did a bag with an apple in it get in my hand?

I make it outside the terminal.... America, my home.... The sun shining on me in my homeland for the first time in over a year felt so amazing. I took a knee an kissed the concrete outside the terminal. It felt so good to be in America again.

From there, I went on my connecting flight, and the actual mid-tour leave story is a story for another time.

After leave....

I arrive in the Dallas airport, and my flight back to Kuwait isn't for another 8 fucking hours. Are you fucking shitting me? I was a 1 hour flight away from Dallas, and I could have potentially spent another 6 hours getting poon?? FTA.

I checked in, and immediately went to the smoking lounge. "Hey! You're that guy that jumped a Bradley!!!" Someone from a different battalion in my brigade recognized me. Had I met him before? I don't even fucking know, but we became insta-buddies. We catch a meal, shoot the shit about how each of our deployments were going. Our brigade was spread out like a shotgun blast across Iraq. The only time we were all in one place was for Samarra.

I fly to Kuwait, and then fly into BIAP. It wasn't until BIAP that I ran into my mechanic buddy again, and my infantry brother from another battalion split from me there. Mechanic and I shoot the shit about leave. He says his leave was boring, I say mine was amazing, and we fly back to Anaconda.

From Anaconda, it was like no one in the army was tracking us. "How are we supposed to get back to our AO?" Figure it out. There's 4 of us, different units, that needed to get back to the same main FOB, but I'm the most ranking individual, so I'm like, "I'll figure this out don't go far."

I find out that we can get ourselves on a flight manifest, and get back to the main FOB. I go back to the area where I told everyone to stick around, aaaannnnnnd.... everyone is gone. I miss the chinook flight out of Anaconda, and find the mechanic buddy. The two other guys saw people from there unit and caught a convoy back up north, but didn't pass along the info. It was just me and the mechanic. We get ourselves on the next chinook flight out of there.

It was night time, and the season had changed. This flight was cold as fuck, holy shit. I pulled out my woobie, and me and this mechanic were fucking cuddle buddies for this flight back to our main FOB. Gay as fuck, bro. We get there, and it's like 01:00 dark as fuck, and cold for fucking Iraq, wtf. We land on the opposite side of the FOB. This was FOB Danger, which was fucking huge. No one from our battalion was there to pick us up from the airfield. Mechanic and I walk around in the dark of the fucking night, no NODs, jjust wandering the fuck around until I see a fucking tent with antennas outside of it. We walk in there, and there's multiple radios set up, and I ask the girl if we can use her radios. I give her the channel to our battalion, and call them up. No one at battalion HQ were even tracking that we were coming in that night. How fucked up is that? They send an HMMWV out to retrieve us, and we get to the palace battalion was at. This was the mechanic's stop, so he said peace. I was stuck there for the night until 2nd platoon from my company rolled through, and I hitched a ride with them back to our FOB.

It was a goat fuck in a half trying to get myself back to the FOB. I don't even know how the Army operated with dipshits like me being told to find their own way back to their AO. Fuck, what if I had been one IQ point lower?
